title: Thin-Seared Salmon Avocado Roll
description: Thin salmon slices cooked through and draped over a creamy avocado-cucumber roll.

ingredients.name: Prepared, seasoned sushi rice
ingredients.note: Use the separate Sushi Rice recipe

steps: Slice salmon against the grain into 2–3 mm slices. Cut avocado and cucumber into slender batons; keep chilled until needed.
In a hot lightly oiled nonstick pan, cook salmon slices briefly on both sides until fully opaque. Work in small batches and transfer to a clean plate; do not leave raw centers.
Spread rice onto half a nori sheet and flip onto a wrapped bamboo mat. Place avocado and cucumber on the nori side and roll tightly.
Overlap fully cooked salmon slices across the exterior; press gently through wrap to secure, then cut eight pieces. Add Kewpie and optional tobiko sparingly.
notes: The thin-searing technique is aburi-inspired, but salmon is cooked through rather than raw beneath the surface.
This baseline yields approximately four rolls (or the equivalent nigiri, gunkan or hand-roll assortment), about six light servings.
Sushi rice is prepared and seasoned separately; the rice quantity here is its ready-to-use weight.
Salmon is fully cooked, including the very thin seared-slice variations; for thicker pieces, 63°C at the center is a conservative target.
